name: Winston Churchill
summary: Churchill defended parliamentary government, constitutional monarchy and private enterprise against socialism, while as a Liberal minister he created trade boards, labour exchanges and unemployment insurance and as a Conservative backed compulsory national insurance and a national health service. He was a lifelong imperialist who ranked peoples and civilisations, resisted Indian independence and supported Zionism, and in foreign policy he championed rearmament, the wartime and Cold War alliance with the United States, a British nuclear deterrent and European unity.

His record as minister answers where it exists (Trade Boards Act 1909, Home Office capital cases and prison reform 1910-1911, the 1919 supplies to the White armies, the Dyer decision 1920, the 1922 Palestine White Paper, the Gold Standard Act 1925, the 1942 bombing directive, Greece 1944, National Service and the steel and road haulage denationalisations of 1952-1953). Answers that rested on Wikipedia were re-sourced or nulled. His Commons speeches 1901-1955 were searched in the local Hansard corpus and historic Hansard by theme: economy (wages, unions, closed shop, nationalisation, controls, taxes, gold, free trade, pensions), government (franchise, electoral systems, Lords, Crown, devolution, referendums), society (women's vote, eugenics, immigration, religion), world (Russia, Palestine, India, Greece, Europe, NATO, the bomb) and liberty (capital punishment, detention). His Gutenberg books (Liberalism and the Social Problem, The River War, My African Journey) were searched by theme. Pages refused to scripted access and left out: IWM's SOE history, the National Archives internment blog and Toye's article on the 1945 Gestapo broadcast (core.ac.uk). The 1954-1955 cabinet discussion of Commonwealth immigration is known only from archive catalogue entries, so immigration statements stay null. Many statements on later or doctrinal topics (the internet, gender identity, Marxist theory, decolonisation doctrine) have no record and stay null.
